taxi.fareNote: Fixed rate from airport; metered in town

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing at Termini, on buses 64/40 and around the Colosseum; the Esquilino area is rougher after dark.

hood_desc: The ancient historic center packed with landmarks like the Pantheon, Trevi Fountain and Piazza Navona amid cobbled streets. Ideal for first-timers who want to walk among Rome's iconic sights.
A charming, bohemian district of ivy-clad lanes, trattorias and lively nightlife across the river. Best for those seeking atmospheric dining and a romantic, local feel.
A trendy, hip neighborhood near the Colosseum with vintage shops, wine bars and artisan boutiques. Suits stylish travelers wanting a cool yet central base.
An elegant, orderly residential area near the Vatican with wide boulevards and good shopping. Great for visitors wanting quieter streets close to St Peters and the Vatican Museums.
A traditional, authentic working-class quarter known for its food scene, market and Roman cuisine. Perfect for food lovers seeking genuine local flavor away from the crowds.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink, including from the city's public drinking fountains (nasoni).

transit.pay: Buy a BIT ticket (€1.50/$1.60, valid 100 minutes) from tobacco shops, station machines, or the MyCicero app, or simply tap a contactless bank card or phone at metro gates and bus validators via ATAC's tap&go system. A 24-hour pass costs €7 (~$7.50).
transit.hours: Metro runs about 5:30am-11:30pm (until 1:30am Fri-Sat); night buses cover the network after the metro closes.

landmarks: Colosseum
The largest ancient amphitheater ever built, its monumental ruined arches make it Rome's single most iconic sight.
Roman Forum
The sprawling ruins of ancient Rome's political and social heart, offering a dramatic sense of the city's classical past.
Pantheon
A remarkably preserved Roman temple famed for its massive coffered dome and oculus, still awe-inspiring after nearly 1,900 years.
Trevi Fountain
Rome's largest and most theatrical Baroque fountain, where tossing a coin is said to guarantee a return to the city.
St. Peter's Basilica
The centerpiece of Vatican City and one of the largest churches in the world, crowned by Michelangelo's soaring dome.
Sistine Chapel
Home to Michelangelo's legendary ceiling frescoes, it's one of the most visited and photographed artistic treasures on earth.
Spanish Steps
A grand 18th-century stairway linking Piazza di Spagna to the Trinità dei Monti church, a favorite spot for people-watching photos.
Piazza Navona
An elegant Baroque square built over an ancient stadium, famous for Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers.
Castel Sant'Angelo
A cylindrical Roman mausoleum-turned-fortress on the Tiber, offering striking views and a dramatic riverside silhouette.
Vatican Museums
A vast museum complex housing masterpieces collected by popes over centuries, including the famed Gallery of Maps and Raphael Rooms.

train.note: Both Nightjet sleepers leave from Roma Termini; Rome has essentially no direct international day trains, so daytime trips abroad mean changing in Milan or Verona. Domestically, Trenitalia and rival Italo (italotreno.com) run frequent high-speed trains, and Trenitalia's Intercity Notte sleepers head overnight to Sicily and Calabria.

bus.note: Most long-distance coaches use the Autostazione Roma Tiburtina next to Tiburtina station, with some services from Anagnina metro station. Carry your passport or EU ID card for cross-border routes.

ferry.note: Rome's port is Civitavecchia, about 80 km northwest — roughly an hour by regional train from Roma Termini. Grimaldi sails to Barcelona around twice a week year-round and to Tunis about weekly (Tunisia's CTN also lists Civitavecchia sailings on some dates — check tunisiaferries.ctn.com.tn). Ferries to Sardinia from Civitavecchia are domestic.

half.name: Pompeii
half.blurb: People flock to this ancient Roman city frozen in time by Mount Vesuvius's famous eruption.

half.name: Tivoli
half.blurb: Visitors come for Villa d'Este's tumbling fountains and Hadrian's Villa, sprawling imperial Roman ruins.

half.name: Florence
half.blurb: The Renaissance cradle lures travelers with its grand Duomo, world-class art, and elegant historic streets.

half.name: Naples
half.blurb: This lively southern city is celebrated for its birthplace pizza, bustling streets, and bayside energy.

half.name: Orvieto
half.blurb: Perched dramatically on a cliff, this hill town is known for its striking golden cathedral.

half.name: Ostia Antica
half.blurb: Rome's remarkably preserved ancient port city lets visitors walk quiet streets among evocative ruins.
